name: device-shadow
context: A constrained or intermittently connected device must be controllable and observable from apps and cloud services even while it is offline. The shadow is a cloud-held JSON document per device that separates what a controller wants (desired) from what the device last reported (reported), plus a computed difference (delta). Because the document lives in the cloud, an app can query and command a device that is not connected; because it carries versions and deltas, the device can reconcile on reconnect rather than replay everything.
benefits: Decouples control from connectivity — apps read and change device state whether or not the device is online
The delta is computed by the service, so each device receives only the attributes that actually differ
Versioning makes out-of-order delivery safe: a device discards any message carrying a version older than the one it tracks
Cloud services keep writing the device's state while it is offline, so the document stays accurate for the next reader
Persistent sessions deliver delta messages on reconnect for devices that are frequently offline
tradeoffs: A shadow is a control-plane document, not a telemetry buffer — high-rate samples belong on the message path, not in a state document
Delta messages can be large; a whole-state delta over a constrained link is expensive unless filtered before delivery
Concurrent conflicting updates resolve by version, not by transaction — a lost update is possible without explicit version checks
The control plane becomes a runtime dependency of every read and write to device state
Wildcard subscriptions to shadow topics are unsafe because the service reserves the right to add topics to the hierarchy
use_cases: Desired-state configuration pushed to devices that reconnect rarely or on cellular links
Mobile apps showing live device state without opening a session to the device
Fleet dashboards reading the last reported state of thousands of devices
Device twins that must survive firmware rollback, with the previous desired state re-applied
Multiple logical shadows per device, separating anonymous telemetry aggregation from operator commands
avoid_when: Data is high-rate telemetry — a state document is the wrong shape and will be constantly rewritten
The device is always connected and the control path is a persistent session — the shadow adds a round trip
Exactly-once command delivery to the device is required, which a versioned document cannot guarantee
Regulatory or operational rules forbid a cloud copy of device state
component_types: Shadow document: JSON with desired, reported and a virtual delta section plus per-attribute metadata timestamps
Shadow type: one unnamed classic shadow, any number of named shadows, plus a reserved named shadow
Reserved MQTT topics: get, update, delete with accepted, rejected, update/delta and update/documents response topics
REST API: the equivalent HTTPS surface, with the same version and clientToken semantics
Client token: a caller-supplied correlation id matching a request to its response over MQTT
Reconnect procedure: apply all deltas, then publish current state as reported
technology_stack: AWS IoT Rules (filter and republish deltas)
anti_patterns: Writing to reported from an app or writing to desired from a device, which breaks the single-writer discipline
Subscribing with a wildcard over shadow topics and being flooded when the service adds new topic stubs
Putting telemetry streams into the shadow document and rewriting the whole document per sample
Applying updates without version preconditions, so a concurrent write silently wins
Not resynchronising on reconnect — a device that never publishes reported state leaves the delta permanently non-empty
design_principles: Desired and reported are written by different actors and never by the same one
The delta is derived, never written — it is the difference between desired and reported
Version every update and treat it as a precondition when concurrent writers are possible
The shadow is the last known state, not a live channel
Filter delta payloads to the attributes the device needs before they cross the link
best_practices: Subscribe to response topics before publishing a request, so accepted/rejected/delta are never missed
Use clientToken to correlate requests and responses in MQTT where delivery order is not guaranteed
On reconnect, read every pending delta and then publish reported state in a single pass
Add a rules-based filter that selects only needed fields and republishes to a device-specific topic
Use named shadows to separate operator commands from anonymous aggregate state
